open.heading:
Someone who
{{actually did it.}}
body: The school runs **Guiding Futures, Shaping Lives** for Classes IX to XII. The 2025 session was taken by **Mr. Ashutosh Kumar Pandey, IRS, Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax**, who shared his own educational journey rather than a careers slide deck.
The measure of a programme like this is who agrees to come and speak as it is — and the school names its guests, with their office, every time.

board.kicker: And the reason for the rooms
board.heading:
Board practicals
{{start here}}
body: Class IX is the year the laboratory programme stops being introductory. Physics, Chemistry and Biology each carry **board practicals from Class IX to Class XII** — the same practicals a board expects a candidate to have done, in rooms built for one subject each.
The syllabus itself is published class by class as [PRECEPT](/academics/philosophy/curriculum/); board outcomes have their own page, [Board Results](/academics/board-results/).

{{Stronger answers.}}

beyond.heading:
Beyond the classroom,
{{inside the school.}}
body: None of the rooms below is added for the board years — they are already there, and Class IX is simply the point at which a student is expected to use all of them.

Every room above is on the school’s own [facilities](/campus/facilities-infrastructure/) inventory; the twelve laboratories are set out on [Laboratories & Academic Clubs](/academics/teaching-learning/laboratories-clubs/).

close.heading:
Board practicals,
{{and a clearer direction.}}
body: Secondary is where preparation meets purpose: three laboratories carrying board practicals from Class IX, a syllabus published class by class, and a serving IRS officer in the hall telling four year groups how he got there. Board outcomes are published separately, and are not restated here.
